claims.claim: Cells require a steady, continuous supply of chemical energy to maintain function and avoid cellular destruction.
Generation and distribution of chemical energy are determining factors in organismal form and function.
Organisms differ from machines because catalysts needed for operation must be generated internally.
Microtubules are differentially sensitive to gravity.
Mechanical forces (adhesion tension, division forces, cytoskeletal waves) significantly contribute to embryonic morphogenesis.
Cell differentiation and morphogenesis are examples of self-organization/entropy reduction.
The first law of thermodynamics states energy cannot be created or destroyed, only transferred or transformed.
Entropy is the unavailability of a system’s thermal energy for conversion into mechanical work and is often interpreted as disorder.
A system in thermodynamic equilibrium has no net flows of mass/energy, no phase changes, and no driving forces.
Evolution is thermodynamically impossible because entropy and evolution are opposing and mutually exclusive concepts.
The second law is an impenetrable barrier that no evolutionary mechanism has overcome.
Living systems are thermodynamically open and far-from-equilibrium systems.
Living cells decrease internal entropy by using an influx of chemical energy and exporting heat and waste.
Pigmented cells contain high amounts of calcium due to melanin’s enormous calcium-binding capacity, exceeding all other tissues.
In skin, melanin is a major determinant of skin color and provides protection against radiation and sun-induced damage including skin cancer.
Melanin’s biological role outside skin (e.g., ocular tissues) is still under intense debate.
Melanin has an intrinsic property to transform visible and invisible light into free chemical energy by dissociating and re-forming water.
Skin pigmentation primarily regulates how much light reaches internal cells to meet metabolic energy needs.
Melanin in trees is located in the trunk and is called lignin.
Of biological pigments, melanin is the most widely distributed in nature across kingdoms.
There is no complete picture of eumelanin macromolecular structure in natural or synthetic form.
EPR/ESR studies provide evidence for semiquinone radicals in eumelanin.
Melanin added to cell culture medium can be taken up into cytosol and subcellular compartments.
Albinism is reduced melanin synthesis rather than total absence, with normal melanocyte numbers in skin and eyes.
Melanin is present in 'albino' Wistar rat ocular tissues in abundant amounts.
Melanin is synthesized in melanosomes; epidermal melanosomes can be degraded after lysosomal fusion into 'melanin dust'.
Neuromelanin accumulates with age in substantia nigra until about 50–60 years then decreases.
Melanin has efficient non-radiative de-excitation that improves when hydrated.
Higher intraocular PO2 in African-American patients than Caucasian patients is indirect evidence that more melanin captures more light and dissipates it via water dissociation/reformation.
Kleiber’s law (metabolic rate scaling approximately as body mass^(3/4)) is universal across life and remains unexplained.
Melanin-driven water dissociation/reformation is the long-sought explanation for Kleiber’s law.
Photoreceptor layer requires about 10× more energy than cerebral cortex and has no blood vessels under normal conditions.
Retinal venous oxygen content is about 38% lower than retinal arterial blood, while choroidal venous-arterial difference is about 3%.
Choroidal blood flow is approximately 27× faster than retinal blood flow.
Water dissociation/reformation by melanin produces a vacuum around vessels that increases blood flow.
The identified melanin reaction is 2H2O ↔ 2H2 + O2 + 4e− occurring in nano-/picoseconds.
Diatomic hydrogen released by melanin is the best known antioxidant and maintains minimal intracellular oxidation.
Melanin is strategically placed in the perinuclear space surrounding the nucleus to regulate metabolic rate.
Melanin absorbs the entire electromagnetic spectrum from radio waves to gamma rays without reflection/refraction.
Chlorophyll irreversibly dissociates water into diatomic hydrogen and oxygen at room temperature.
Human photosynthesis is more efficient than plant photosynthesis because it both dissociates and re-forms water, yielding four high-energy electrons per two re-formed water molecules.
Glucose is not an energy source; it is only a biomass precursor.
Mitchell’s chemiosmotic theory for mitochondrial ATP production remains unresolved and is still just a theory.
The human body requires roughly 50–180 kg of ATP daily while containing about 50 g at any moment, implying rapid recycling.

The ability to dissociate water decreases from age 26 by about 10% per decade and falls sharply after the 50s; it also decreases with cold, contaminated water, iron supplements, alcohol, anesthetics, antidepressants, pesticides, herbicides, and certain drugs.
Inadequate melanin-driven photosynthesis is the major reason diseases develop.
Pharmacologic intensification of human photosynthesis improved age-related macular degeneration anatomy within 8 weeks in an example case.
Pharmacologic intensification of human photosynthesis produced remarkable improvement in an Alzheimer’s disease case over 8 months.
Alzheimer’s disease is fundamentally an energy problem rather than a biomass problem.
Preventive and curative medicine will be transformed by pharmacologically modulating melanin-mediated water dissociation/reformation.

concepts.definition: A state with no net macroscopic flows and no driving gradients (thermal, mechanical, chemical, radiative) within the system.
A thermodynamic state function quantifying energy dispersal; constrains directionality of processes and relates to reversible heat transfer by dS = δQ_rev/T.
A system exchanging energy/matter with its environment and maintained away from equilibrium by fluxes, enabling local order formation with net entropy export.
Deterministic dynamics where small differences in initial conditions can yield large differences in outcomes, limiting predictability.
Empirical allometric scaling of basal metabolic rate with body mass, often approximated as E ∝ M^(3/4) across many taxa.
The unresolved detailed supramolecular organization and structure–property mapping of eumelanin due to chemical and morphological heterogeneity.
Persistent paramagnetic signals attributed to semiquinone-like moieties embedded within melanin materials.
ATP synthesis driven by proton-motive force across the inner mitochondrial membrane via ATP synthase.
Proposed light-driven reversible reaction 2H2O ↔ 2H2 + O2 + 4e− mediated by melanin in human tissues to supply cellular free chemical energy.
Proposed mechanism that melanin photochemistry sets cellular metabolic rate and explains cross-species metabolic scaling.
Proposed identity of plant lignin with melanin located in tree trunks.

logical_flow: Cellular requirement -> Continuous free chemical energy is necessary for coordinated intracellular work and maintenance of order.
Thermodynamic framing -> Second law is interpreted as forcing disorder; evolution is asserted to require an opposing ordering principle.
Search for ordering principle -> A universal conserved mechanism is posited to reconcile biological complexity with entropy.
Candidate selection -> Melanin is chosen due to ubiquity, optical absorption, redox/radical properties, and anatomical placement (notably in eye).
Mechanism proposal -> Light absorbed by melanin drives reversible water dissociation/reformation producing H2, O2, and electrons, yielding free chemical energy.
Indirect supports -> Persistent EPR radicals, oxygen consumption, ocular PO2 differences, and avascular photoreceptors near melanin-rich tissues are treated as consistent with the mechanism.
Unification -> The mechanism is proposed to explain Kleiber’s law and universal metabolic regulation across life.
Bioenergetic revision -> Glucose is reassigned to biomass only; ATP-centric and chemiosmotic explanations are deemed insufficient.
Disease model -> Disease is attributed primarily to declining melanin-driven water dissociation (age and exposures).
Translational implication -> Pharmacologic enhancement of the melanin-water reaction is proposed for prevention and treatment (e.g., AMD, AD).
